text.p: - Franc Rode was elected as Slovenia's new archbishop, the Holy Seat said on Wednesday.

- Some 20 percent of Slovenians think Rode is the right person for the job, about 25 percent said they did not know the candidate well enough, while some 40 percent had no opinion, a survey made by daily Delo showed.

- Janez Podobnik, Slovenian parliamentary president, continues his three-day visit to Belgium where he is meeting European counterparts to try to gain support for the country's efforts to join the EU.
- Four people near Rogaska Slatina, 110 km (67 miles) east of Ljubljana, were murdered by an unknown assailant in one of the biggest crimes in Slovenia's history.

- Only around six percent of Slovenians think large forestry estates nationalised after the World War Two should be returned to their owners, according to a survey by Delo. About 57 percent of Slovenians say nationals should get their land back but not foreigners who previously owned estates.
- The centre-left Liberal Democrats said that a referendum was likely on whether to limit the number of forest areas nationalised after the second World War to be returned to their previous owners.
- The Slovenian coal-mines association pushed the government to increase prices of domestic coal by 15 percent, in order to protect domestic coal production.
- Representatives of Slovenian scientists signed a cooperation agreement with their Italian colleagues in Rome on Wednesday.
